scope: Core content only; assignments and optional/supporting readings excluded. Guided practice inside core pages is included. Opening context and parent/child development are read together. Footnotes excluded from subsection screening; prior published counts include them and are triage only. Short blocks were reviewed in context; a numerical threshold is not a verdict.
review_method: Inventory of all 84 core pages and their heading hierarchy, followed by contextual reading of flagged passages, ancestors, neighboring sections, examples and local practice. This is a depth/organization audit, not certification of every code cell, factual claim or index entry.
verification: Targeted .NET 10.0.107 run: untrimmed integer parse true/98; retained array loop 345 vs complete sum 433. No full code rerun or fresh build.

excluded.title: Optional: Escaped Identifiers and Contextual Keywords

findings.heading: The `var` Keyword
findings.already_adequate: The declaration examples establish that the compiler infers a type.
findings.gap: The 38-word subsection does not make the inferred type versus later reassignment distinction explicit.
findings.proposal: Add an annotated initializer-to-inferred-type trace and a predict/explain check contrasting a valid reassignment with assigning a different type. Do not introduce dynamic typing as a new topic.

findings.heading: Operation Examples
findings.already_adequate: Operator definitions, category tables, runnable examples, comments, and short-circuit rules already exist.
findings.gap: Definitions and examples are separated. Arithmetic, Comparison, and Logical demonstration blocks have only 7-9 prose words around code; the broader surrounding explanation does not interpret these particular results.
findings.proposal: Pair each essential category with its existing worked cell, interpret selected intermediate values and results, and add one bounded prediction. Keep the comprehensive table as a later reference within the lesson. No exercise quota per operator.

findings.heading: Compare Ways to Express the Same Decision
findings.already_adequate: The service-code decision table, switch example, invalid-case explanation, and guided variation are useful.
findings.gap: The lesson compares if/else-if and switch before the later sections develop the basic selection forms. Local practice is weighted toward modifying supplied examples rather than choosing and tracing branches.
findings.proposal: Keep the business problem/table as framing. Develop if, if/else, else-if, nesting and switch, then use the existing cross-form comparison as synthesis. Add a first-match-versus-independent-if trace and a boundary/invalid-case completion. Chapter 2 already explains short-circuit evaluation; reuse it rather than claiming it is absent.

findings.heading: Connect Calls, Definitions, and Program Forms
findings.already_adequate: The page has a conceptual motivation, program-form comparison, method definitions/signatures, call flow, and guided practice.
findings.gap: One subsection spans roughly 2,460 inclusive prose words. Its direct text repeats reasons for methods and terminology before separate definition, signature, and execution-flow children; top-level and class-based forms compete for attention.
findings.proposal: Use one task and top-level helper as the main sequence: definition, call, arguments/parameters, execution/return. Group the retained class-member/Main forms as clearly bounded project comparison after that sequence. Preserve the distinct examples and traces.

findings.heading: Step 2: Minimize the Failing Case
findings.already_adequate: The later Credits example supplies a complete familiar-loop investigation, expected result, breakpoint trace, repair and regression checks.
findings.gap: The first detailed workflow example uses scores arrays before arrays are taught in Chapter 7. The familiar-loop treatment appears later, despite describing itself as preparation before array applications.
findings.proposal: Move the familiar-loop investigation into the first workflow demonstration and map the workflow steps onto it. Retain the array/CSV transfers after it with explicit later-prerequisite labels; do not count them as needed to understand the core debugger process. Correct the ambiguous retained loop comment during an authorized repair.

findings.heading: Parameters to Main
findings.already_adequate: Array parameter behavior, command-line arguments and aliases all have developed explanations.
findings.gap: The Parameters to Main/Command Line Adder group occupies about 896 inclusive words between passing-array instruction and References and Aliases. This interrupts the parameter/sharing conceptual dependency.
findings.proposal: Teach traversal, passing arrays, reference copying/aliasing and mutation together. Put the command-line application after that complete sequence, with a transition showing it applies the same array model. Preserve its project workflow and examples.

findings.heading: Similar Operations, Different Methods
findings.already_adequate: The family map and operations tables explain meaningful differences; list/dictionary lessons develop the main APIs.
findings.gap: The 4,019-word operations page presents a long general/namespace/table sequence before the family-specific examples, then revisits related families. Its length is largely sequencing and reference breadth, not a missing-concept problem.
findings.proposal: Retain a compact conceptual map first. Pair the shared put/inspect/remove rules with an early concrete list/dictionary comparison, then attach each existing family example to the relevant table row. Keep later-family recognition distinct from the current implementation focus, without silently changing core prerequisites.

findings.heading: Splitting and Tokenizing / Token Validation
findings.already_adequate: The split/trim examples, missing-field warning and later Structured Lines parser are substantive.
findings.gap: The text incorrectly says int.TryParse would fail for " 98 " until trimmed. The Token Validation subsection has 11 prose words and a valid-record-only cell, which never enters its rejection branch.
findings.proposal: Correct the whitespace explanation and distinguish normalization, field count, numeric parsing and domain validation. Add a short accepted/rejected record trace, including missing and extra fields; connect it to the existing parser instead of adding another full implementation. Verified locally: int.TryParse(" 98 ", out int score) returns true with 98 on .NET 10.

findings.heading: Tuples: When a Class Is Too Much
findings.already_adequate: Tuple syntax, creation, returns, deconstruction/discards, collections and a tuple/class comparison already exist.
findings.gap: Four child topics have 22-41 prose words before their runnable examples and no following prose interpretation. The SalesRange example indexes element zero without stating a nonempty-input contract.
findings.proposal: Explain how a returned tuple maps into named fields and deconstructed variables, interpret one transcript, state the nonempty-array assumption or a chosen empty policy, and add one bounded completion with feedback. Preserve tuples as the bridge used by later examples.

findings.heading: Copies Need a Depth Policy
findings.already_adequate: Identity, assignment, mutability and copy-depth policy are explicitly explained. The following records page correctly warns that with is shallow.
findings.gap: The copy-depth subsection explains an order/product graph verbally but does not work through the nested-sharing case as an actual object diagram or before/after trace.
findings.proposal: Add one small shared-product/two-orders diagram and a table of which observations change after a nested mutation or shallow copy. Reuse it from the records and composition pages; no new full program or blanket chapter expansion is needed.

findings.heading: Virtual Calls Select an Override
findings.already_adequate: The core already has concrete overrides, predicted numeric output, constructor examples, interfaces, test doubles and local exercises.
findings.gap: The declared-type/runtime-type distinction is explained mostly in prose. The local final practice checks result bounds using already-supplied overrides rather than requiring the learner to follow dispatch choices.
findings.proposal: Add a small declared type / actual object / selected member / base call / result table and a prediction before revealing it. Keep the three core readings; low total words alone do not justify a broad expansion or importing optional hiding examples.

findings.action: Expand a prerequisite bridge and clarify organization
findings.heading: Reading Short Expressions and Queries
findings.already_adequate: Generic methods/classes/constraints/interfaces and iterators now have substantial explanation and local tracing/completion practice.
findings.gap: The compact bridge introduces lambda syntax, Where, Select, OrderBy, ToArray, deferred execution, expression-bodied members and target-typed new in about 138 prose words. These are several distinct forms for an introductory CS2 transition.
findings.proposal: Give one explicit loop-to-pipeline worked comparison with intermediate values and a deferred/materialized prediction. Place syntax reminders at first later use. Keep the generic/iterator lessons intact; distinguish the hand-written enumerator comparison from the basic yield path. The 35-40-minute-per-reading claim for four readings also conflicts with the 110-minute chapter allocation and needs a coherent meeting map.

findings.heading: References Are Paths, Not Copies / Insertion Order and Lost Links
findings.already_adequate: The chapter now has strong pointer explanations, update traces, a sentinel comparison, complete implementations and local practice.
findings.gap: The cursor/reference diagram and lost-link trace come after the first traversal, insertion and deletion examples. The alternative header-node model is introduced before the complete no-sentinel sequence, requiring a representation switch and switch back.
findings.proposal: Move reference/cursor interpretation before traversal and attach the lost-link trace to the first insertion. Complete one representation before comparing the sentinel alternative. Preserve both complete treatments and the exercises.

findings.heading: Connected Components and Direction / Components and Direction
findings.already_adequate: DFS frames, reachability, component examples and verification contracts are developed.
findings.gap: Two nearby subsections repeat the directed-versus-undirected component distinction. The second 48-word block partly refers onward rather than advancing the current explanation.
findings.proposal: Combine the direction rules and existing small counterexample into one comparison before the component implementation. Keep frame/enter-exit tracing first and verification as the concluding synthesis. Preserve distinct contracts, examples and old anchors.

findings.heading: Shortest Paths and Dijkstra
findings.already_adequate: The distance trace, relaxation completion, stale-entry argument, path witness checks and model comparison are substantive.
findings.gap: The reading includes 1,274 code lines across demonstrations, starters and hidden answers, with repeated approximately 100-line standalone classes. Full verification infrastructure competes visually with the central settle/relax/path reasoning.
findings.proposal: Organize the reading as one focused algorithm narrative followed by a clearly labeled full implementation and verification reference. Keep independent execution by supplying complete setup in each runnable unit; use collapsible support or a downloadable project rather than removing declarations or creating hidden state. Do not delete the boundary cases or correctness arguments.
